clue.text: Moralising story quietly disposed of a form of farming

definitions.note: ARABLE is an adjective; the clue treats arable farming as its noun

indicators.note: something disposed of is got rid of, so the musical abbreviation for quiet is thrown out of the word

blocks.note: a parable is a short story with a moral
P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: A preachy fable about some kind of farming has been thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: PARABLE loses its P to leave ARABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable farming grows crops on ploughed land, as opposed to raising livestock, so arable names that kind of agriculture.

clue.text: Feeling height? Learner will be tense

indicators.note: saying one thing will be another tells us to swap the first letter for the second within the word

blocks.note: altitude is height above sea level
L is the learner driver's plate
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A nervous novice afraid of heights will be tense.
explanation.walkthrough: In ALTITUDE the L becomes a T, giving ATTITUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An attitude is a settled way of thinking or feeling about something, so feeling serves as a synonym.

clue.text: Appropriate prisoner is about to enter destined term of life

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so these pieces are placed within the next word

blocks.note: con is short for convict
fate is the lot destined for one's life; it wraps around the next pieces
taken as written
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A convict is about to begin a life sentence that was always coming to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' is the verb meaning to seize, not the adjective meaning suitable; the two pieces after the prisoner sit together inside the destined lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate is to take something for oneself, and to confiscate is to seize property with official authority.

clue.text: A piece of cake is like this — fatty but not gross

definitions.text: A piece of cake is like this

indicators.note: but not asks for one word with something taken away from it

blocks.note: greasy food is fatty
GR is the standard abbreviation for gross

explanation.surface: A slice of cake described as fatty without being disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: GREASY minus GR leaves EASY. 'A piece of cake' is the idiom for a simple task, not a slice of sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is a piece of cake is an idiom meaning it is simple to do, so the task is easy.

clue.text: Routine he can claim needs to be changed

indicators.note: a thing that needs to be changed must be altered, so these letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A man's ordinary insurance claim has to be amended.
explanation.definitionFit: Routine actions are done automatically without thought, which is what mechanical means when used of behaviour.

clue.text: Bishop behind singer

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
ass is American slang for the behind, the backside

explanation.surface: A bishop stands at the back of a chorister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a position word but supplies the backside, ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass is a singer with the lowest male voice range in a choir.

clue.text: Bloke for example covering a wine cellar

indicators.note: in a down entry, covering means sitting on top of, so the earlier pieces are placed above the later one

blocks.note: bod is British slang for a person, a bloke
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man, say, putting a lid over a wine store.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine cellar or wine shop, so the definition is a direct translation.

clue.text: Chaps declare their schmutter

blocks.note: chaps are men
to swear is to declare under oath

explanation.surface: Men announcing what they are wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Schmutter is British slang, from Yiddish, for clothing; 'their' points back to the chaps, so the clothes are men's.
explanation.definitionFit: Menswear is clothing made for men, and schmutter is a slang word for clothes.

clue.text: Reason to share beer

blocks.note: a ration is a fixed share
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: An excuse to split a pint between friends.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying reason or justification for a course of action.

clue.text: Stood up by a prickly paragon?

blocks.note: taken as written
a rose is a thorny flower, and an English rose is a byword for beauty

explanation.surface: Jilted on a date by a thorny beauty, with a question mark flagging the joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stood up' sounds like being jilted, but here it is simply the past tense of rising.
explanation.definitionFit: Arose is the past tense of arise, meaning got up or rose to one's feet.

clue.text: In short, sharp cheese is first

indicators.note: is first fixes the order, putting the cheese before the other piece

blocks.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
fly is British slang for sharp or knowing

explanation.surface: A pungent cheese should come first on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefly and in short are both phrases meaning to put it concisely.

clue.text: She waits on street getting into scrapes with son

indicators.note: getting into means going inside, so the abbreviation is put within the word for scrapes

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
to hoe is to scrape the soil with a garden tool
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A woman waits in the street and keeps getting into trouble along with her boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrapes' looks like trouble, but it is the verb for working soil with a garden hoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostess is a woman who attends to guests, serving them as a host does.

clue.text: Female ignored storm about long-legged bird

indicators.note: about suggests turning round, so the word for storm is read backwards
something ignored is left out, so the female abbreviation is dropped

blocks.note: to fume is to rage, to storm
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman takes no notice of a long-legged bird raging around.
explanation.walkthrough: FUME reversed is EMUF; dropping the F leaves EMU.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian bird with long powerful legs.

clue.text: Preserving prayer is a redeeming feature

blocks.note: saving means keeping or preserving
grace is a short prayer said before a meal

explanation.surface: A prayer that keeps one safe is a point in one's favour.
explanation.definitionFit: A saving grace is one good quality that makes up for someone's other failings.

clue.text: Charmer I bear with difficulty, over time one bleeds you dry

indicators.note: something done with difficulty is done awkwardly, so these letters come out jumbled
in a down entry, over means placed above, so the earlier letters sit on top of the last one

blocks.note: a vamp is a seductive woman, a charmer
these letters rearranged
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A seductive person I put up with grudgingly, until in time they exploit me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One bleeds you dry' sounds figurative, about a sponger, but the vampire bat literally feeds on blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A vampire bat is a Latin American bat that feeds on the blood of animals, draining its victims.

clue.text: Manager we'd reappointed — one tends to the wild side of life

definitions.text: one tends to the wild side of life

indicators.note: reappointed suggests something set up again in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A manager we brought back is one who looks after the rowdier aspects of existence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The wild side of life' sounds like partying; it is wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: A game warden is an official who protects wild animals and enforces hunting rules on a reserve.

clue.text: Locality giving home to new venue

indicators.note: giving home to means housing something, so one word is placed inside the other

blocks.note: an area is a locality
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood that accommodates a newly built place for events.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed space for sports or shows, a kind of venue.

clue.text: Jack's plot is not practical

blocks.note: a jack is a sailor, an AB or able seaman, here with the possessive S
a tract is a plot or stretch of land

explanation.surface: Somebody's scheme is unworkable.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack (as in jack tar) is an old name for a sailor, and AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstract means theoretical, concerned with ideas rather than with practical matters.

clue.text: Model's first with current coat

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of that word

blocks.note: the initial of the word
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: A fashion model's leading piece of clothing paired with a coat that is in fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A mac, short for mackintosh, is a British word for a waterproof raincoat.

clue.text: Make fast ship loaded with tons put on speed

indicators.note: a vessel loaded with cargo holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to moor a ship is to tie it up securely
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: A vessel tied up and heavily laden, then told to go faster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make fast' means secure, not hurry; the speed is in the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To motor is to drive along quickly, so to put on speed in a vehicle.

clue.text: Young 'un who's spotted brewing green tea

indicators.note: brewing means being stirred up or prepared, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A youngster seen making a cup of green tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' seems to mean seen, but it means pimply, the stereotype of a spotty adolescent.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a young person aged 13 to 19, often teased for having acne spots.

clue.text: Relative realist wins weirdly

indicators.note: weirdly means in a strange way, so the letters appear in a strange order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A family member who takes a down-to-earth view somehow comes out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A sister-in-law is a relative by marriage, the sister of one's spouse or the wife of one's brother.

clue.text: Any minute now outside a large bar

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so one phrase's word goes around the other letters

blocks.note: soon means any minute now
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Shortly we will be standing outside a big pub.
explanation.walkthrough: SOON goes around A and L: S-AL-OON.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon is a bar; in Britain the saloon bar was the more comfortable room of a pub.

clue.text: A long time in general

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the following word

blocks.note: the letters at the end of the word

explanation.surface: A long time, broadly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In general' reads as a stock phrase, but 'in' signals that the answer lies inside 'general'.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long and distinct period of history.

clue.text: A place to go for assets

blocks.note: taken as written
the gents is a British name for a men's public toilet, a euphemistic place to go

explanation.surface: Somewhere to visit when looking for valuable holdings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assets' sounds financial, but in espionage an asset is a spy working for one's side.
explanation.definitionFit: In intelligence jargon an asset is a source or spy, which is what secret agents are.

clue.text: Set free from concerning contract

blocks.note: re means concerning, about
a lease is a rental contract

explanation.surface: Released from the terms of an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To release someone is to let them go, liberating them from confinement.

clue.text: One term for conker tree

blocks.note: first meaning: one who aces others, a conqueror, with conker played as a sound-alike of conquer
second meaning: the botanical genus of maples and sycamores

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the horse chestnut, which drops conkers, but that is not an acer; the first half is a pun on conker as conqueror, someone who aces opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the genus name for maples, a common ornamental tree in gardens.

clue.text: Check rant in flood of criticism, say

blocks.note: to bar is to check or block
to rage is to rant

explanation.surface: Holding back a tirade amid a torrent of complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks the definition as an example: a flood of criticism is one kind of barrage.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a rapid overwhelming outpouring, as of questions or complaints, from the sense of continuous artillery fire.

clue.text: Book blooming booze-up

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
flowers that are out are in bloom

explanation.surface: A book about a drinking session, with blooming as a mild British curse.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout is a spell of activity, and a drinking bout is a booze-up, a heavy session of drinking.

clue.text: Picked Charlie with socks

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
hose is an old word for stockings or socks

explanation.surface: A man named Charlie selected along with his socks.
explanation.definitionFit: Chose is the past tense of choose, meaning selected or picked out.

clue.text: New menu with meat's fun

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the letters are made into a different arrangement

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A restaurant's new menu featuring meat is a delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusement is enjoyment or entertainment, which is what fun provides.
